chapter_theme: One song at Odukkaththu Cherivay (ஒடுக்கத்துச் செறிவாய்): the courtesans' arts, love potions, smiles with stained teeth, the gold assayed in their hands and the quarrel that sends a man away; the praise names Vishnu at length and Murugan who came as a merchant to esteem Tamil.

987.reading: The poet describes courtesans versed in deceitful talk and the arts of Kama, who feed men herbal potions, melt and cheat hard-hearted fools, speak base words, hug a man's neck, laugh showing stained teeth, take the wealth from his hand and assay its gold, count the hours and pick a quarrel to drive him off, and asks whether he will not rid himself of the ruined mind that enters their arts. The praise names Murugan who crushed the demons and wedded the hunter girl, Vishnu who lies on the serpent in the sea and stretched his hand into the butter-pot, and Murugan as the one who came as a merchant to honour Tamil, at Odukkaththu Cherivay.
987.nuance: மருத்துப் பச்சிலை தீற்று: the women dose their men with herbal love-potions, a rarer charge than flattery. கற்புகர் மாற்று உரைப்பது: they test the touchstone value of the gold they take, the bargain made exact. உரைக்கச் செட்டியனாய்ப் பன் முத்தமிழ் மதித்திட்டு: Murugan coming as a merchant to esteem Tamil points to a local story the text does not tell, and the lines on the Tamil-learned one (தமிழ் தேர்த்த வித்தகர்) are hard to divide.

links.note: The Kural's women weigh the profit before they speak of virtue; 987 makes the weighing literal, the courtesans assaying the gold they take and counting the hours before the quarrel that ends the bargain.
